newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec movie director and actress die in plane crash. [CORRECTED 19:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Quebec movie director and actress die in plane crash. [CORRECTED 19:40 GMT]

text.p: Award-winning Quebec movie director Jean-Claude Lauzon and his actress girlfriend Marie-Soleil Tougas were killed in a weekend plane crash in northern Quebec, authorities said on Monday.

Lauzon, 44, was best known in the French-speaking Canadian province of Quebec and in France for his movies "Un zoo la nuit" and "Leolo". "Un zoo la nuit" won 13 Genie awards - Canada's version of the Oscars -- in 1988.
Tougas, 27, was a popular co-anchor of the Quebec-France television program "Fort Boyard" and had acted in many popular Quebec TV soaps since she was a child.

Quebec provincial police spokesman Pierre Robichaud said Lauzon and Tougas were on vacation when their Cessna 180, piloted by Lauzon, crashed on Sunday in a remote area about 1,500 km (932.1 miles) north of Montreal (corrects distance).
"They both died instantly," Robichaud said. The couple were the only people aboard the plane.
Robichaud said the cause of the crash was under investigation. The bodies were expected to be returned to Montreal later on Monday.
